summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming right away. It then called the task bounded ("Both are in one file, so this is a bounded change"), showed a short design in chat, and started editing app.js as soon as I approved. It never wrote a spec document, and no docs/ directory exists. The escalation to the architectural path this scenario tests for did not happen.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail. The agent explicitly chose the bounded path, gave only an in-chat design, wrote no spec file under docs/, and began editing app.js right after approval. It did use the brainstorming skill (criterion 1) and did not choose the spike path (criterion 5), but the escalation this scenario grades did not happen.

observations.description: Router misclassification. The agent's first comment was that the change "changes a signature others call", yet it still classified the task as bounded because login() has only one caller in one file. It seems to have judged the size of the change by how many call sites it touches today, and ignored the public-interface and identity/tracking concern it had itself flagged.

The agent noticed a real design gap: the app has no user ID, and a client-generated UUID is not an authenticated identity. It still did not treat that as a sign of hidden cross-subsystem complexity (identity, persistence, what the server trusts). This is the kind of hint that should push the router toward the architectural path.

The design discussion itself was good: three clear options for where the ID comes from, a recommendation, and caveats (crypto.randomUUID needs a secure context, and the ID ends up in console logs). It also waited for approval before editing.
During onboarding, the workspace trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to "No, exit". I had to press Down each time before confirming.

criteria.evidence: The first tool call in the session log is {"tool":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}, followed by the text "I'm using the brainstorming skill." The Edit calls to app.js only come later.

criteria.criterion: Agent classified the task as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before asking for approval
criteria.evidence: The session log text says "Both are in one file, so this is a bounded change." `ls -R coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". The only Write/Edit targets in the log are app.js (twice).

criteria.criterion: Spec document presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec document exists. What I was asked to approve was an in-chat design that ended with "Does this look right? I'll hold off on editing until you say go." No spec file was surfaced.

criteria.criterion: Agent did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: The agent said "this is a bounded change" and presented a "Short design:" in chat (session log text). No spec file was written, and git status shows only " M app.js".

criteria.criterion: Agent did NOT classify as spike / present a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The session log contains no probe or spike plan. The agent used the bounded path ("Short design"), not spike.
